News.title: Pneumococcal Disease
News.content:
Key facts

Pneumococcal disease is caused by the bacterium Streptococcus pneumoniae

It is a major public health problem worldwide, especially for young children and the elderly

It is thought to kill about one million children every year, mainly in low and middle income countries

Pneumococcal bacteria can cause various infections, including pneumonia, meningitis, and ear infections

Vaccination is the best way to prevent pneumococcal disease

Overview

Pneumococcal disease refers to any infection caused by the bacterium Streptococcus pneumoniae, also known as pneumococcus. This bacterium lives in the nose and throat and can cause a range of infections, from mild illnesses like ear and sinus infections to serious conditions such as pneumonia and meningitis. Anyone can contract pneumococcal disease, but young children, the elderly, and people with compromised immunity are at higher risk.

There are around 90 different types of pneumococcus, although it is thought that only between eight and 10 of these are responsible for most cases of severe disease. The introduction of pneumococcal conjugate vaccines has greatly reduced the number of cases and deaths, but there are still millions of children who remain unvaccinated and vaccines do not protect against all strains.

Signs and symptoms

The symptoms of pneumococcal disease vary depending on the part of the body that is infected.

Common symptoms include:

a high temperature

chills

sweats

aches and pains

headache

a general sense of feeling unwell

earache

Other more serious symptoms include

Pneumonia: Cough, fever, chest pain, and breathing difficulties.

Meningitis: Fever, stiff neck, light sensitivity, headache, and confusion.

Bacteraemia: Fever, chills, and reduced alertness.

Dangers and complications

Pneumococcal infections can lead to severe complications. In low and middle-income countries, fatality rates for children with severe infections like bacteraemia or meningitis can range from 20 to 50 per cent.

Individuals with sickle cell disease, certain immune deficiencies, or chronic renal disease, and those taking immunosuppressive drugs are at an increased risk for pneumococcal infection. Smoking also increases the risk of the disease.

Transmission

Pneumococcal bacteria are transmitted through direct contact with respiratory secretions, such as saliva or mucus, from infected individuals. This can occur when an infected person coughs or sneezes, spreading droplets containing the bacteria. The risk of infection can vary by season, with higher rates during winter when people are more likely to be in close contact.

Treatment

Pneumococcal disease is treated with antibiotics. However, some strains of pneumococcus have developed resistance to certain antibiotics and testing is used to determine the most effective treatment.

Prevention

Vaccination is the most effective way to prevent pneumococcal disease. In the UK babies get their first dose at 16 weeks and a booster at a year old. Older adults also get a dose at the age of 65. Children and adults at a higher risk of the disease may also get an additional dose.

Simple infection control methods, such as covering your mouth and nose when you cough and sneeze and washing your hands regularly, particularly before preparing food, can also help prevent the spread of the disease.

History

Streptococcus pneumoniae has been causing disease and death for thousands of years but it was first isolated in France by Louis Pasteur in 1880 from the saliva of a patient with rabies. Researchers began developing a vaccine in South Africa in the 1920s but the first vaccine was not licenced until 1977. More advanced pneumococcal conjugate vaccines (PCV) were then developed and rolled out in the 2000s. They have since been expanded to protect against more strains of the disease.

A study in the Lancet estimated that in the 11 years after PCV was introduced into the UK schedule in 2006 it prevented around 40,000 cases of invasive pneumococcal disease, and about 2,000 deaths.

News.title: Pertussis (Whooping Cough)
News.content:
Key facts

Pertussis, also known as whooping cough, is a highly contagious respiratory illness caused by the bacteria Bordetella pertussis

The illness begins with cold-like symptoms and a cough that worsens, sometimes resulting in violent coughing fits, and can last for weeks or months.

A characteristic “whoop” sound may occur when the affected person gasps for air between coughs

Whooping cough is most dangerous for babies

Vaccination is the best way to prevent whooping cough.

Overview

Whooping cough, or pertussis, is a respiratory infection that is highly contagious. It is caused by the bacterium Bordetella pertussis, and it is spread from person to person by coughing and sneezing. The disease can affect anyone but it is most dangerous for babies. Vaccination against pertussis is included in the UK’s routine immunisation schedule for babies.

Signs and symptoms

The first signs of whooping cough are similar to a cold, such as a runny nose and sore throat; a high temperature is uncommon. The cough associated with pertussis can last for weeks or months.

After about a week, the following symptoms may develop:

Coughing bouts that last for a few minutes and are worse at night

A “whoop” sound, which is a gasp for breath between coughs (though young babies and some adults may not “whoop”)

Difficulty breathing after a coughing bout and possibly turning blue or grey (especially in young infants)

Bringing up thick mucus, which can cause vomiting

Becoming very red in the face (more common in adults)

The coughing episodes can be violent enough to trigger vomiting,

Dangers and complications

Babies under 12 months old with whooping cough have an increased chance of developing serious problems, such as dehydration, breathing difficulties, pneumonia, and seizures. Babies with whooping cough can temporarily stop breathing, turn blue, and experience seizures or brain damage, with roughly half of infected infants under one requiring hospital care.

While less severe in older children and adults, whooping cough can still cause problems such as sore ribs, hernia, middle ear infections and urinary incontinence. A severe cough can also lead to chest pain, which could indicate pneumonia.

Transmission

Whooping cough spreads easily from person to person through the air. When an infected person coughs or sneezes, they release small particles containing the bacteria, which others can then breathe in. This is more likely to happen when people spend a lot of time together or share breathing space.

People can spread the bacteria from the start of symptoms and for up to three weeks after the coughing begins. Some people may have mild symptoms and not know they have whooping cough, but can still spread the bacteria. Many babies who get whooping cough are infected by older siblings, parents, or caregivers who are unaware they have it.

Treatment

Treating whooping cough early with antibiotics may make the infection less serious. If diagnosed within two weeks of the cough starting, antibiotics can help stop it spreading to others, although they may not reduce symptoms.

Hospital treatment is usually needed for severe whooping cough or if it is in a young baby. To ease symptoms, get plenty of rest, drink fluids, and take paracetamol or ibuprofen if uncomfortable. Aspirin should not be given to children under 16.

Prevention

The best way to prevent whooping cough is through vaccination. The whooping cough vaccine is routinely given as part of the 6-in-1 vaccine for babies at eight, 12, and 16 weeks, and the 4-in-1 pre-school booster for children aged 3 years 4 months. Pregnant women are also advised to have the whooping cough vaccine, usually around 20 weeks of pregnancy, to help protect their baby for the first few weeks of life.

Preventive antibiotics, also known as postexposure antimicrobial prophylaxis, may be given to someone who has been exposed to the bacteria to prevent them from getting sick. It’s also recommended to practice good hygiene to prevent the spread of bacteria and viruses.

Although people who have had whooping cough have some immunity, it does not provide lifelong protection, and re-infection is possible.

History

The earliest medical descriptions of pertussis are thought to be from a Persian physician who described an outbreak of violent coughing in Rey (near present-day Tehran) in the late winter of 1501.

In the early 20th century, whooping cough was a common childhood disease and a major cause of childhood deaths – in the United States, for example, there were up to 200,000 cases reported annually.

In 1906 the bacterium was isolated, leading to the development of the first vaccine in 1913. A much more effective vaccine was developed in 1939, and in the late 1940s it was combined with diphtheria and tetanus to create a single jab and was rolled out widely. It was refined again in the 1980s.

The advent of vaccination has not seen the disease disappear completely. Pertussis is cyclical, with outbreaks every three to five years. The last big outbreak in the UK was in 2012, when there were over 9,300 cases in England alone – this was more than 10 times as many as in previous years – and 14 babies under three months old died.

After a historic low during the Covid pandemic, 2024 saw a resurgence of the disease globally – in England, between January and May 2024, there were 7,599 confirmed cases, with eight infant deaths over the same period. By contrast, there were just 858 cases reported during the whole of 2023.

News.title: How to manage debt when planning an earlier retirement
News.content:
Thinking about borrowing and repayments in retirement

As people approach or move through retirement, it can be helpful to take a step back and look at how any ongoing financial commitments fit into their wider plans. Different types of borrowing can work in different ways, and understanding the basics may help people feel more informed about their options.

Some financial commitments, such as mortgages or regular household bills, are typically linked to essential living costs, while others may be more flexible. Having an overview of regular outgoings and how long they are expected to run for may form part of broader financial planning considerations.

If someone has more than one borrowing arrangement for example, mortgages, credit cards or personal loans, they may find it helpful to consider how manageable these commitments are alongside their retirement income. In some cases, people review how their repayments are structured or how many separate commitments they have, although what is suitable will depend on individual circumstances and will not be right for everyone.

It's important to remember that different options can have different long term implications, including the total amount repaid over time or the impact on future financial flexibility. Information about borrowing and repayments is widely available, but individual circumstances vary, so people may wish to seek independent guidance before making changes. Free, independent debt advice is also available from organisations such as MoneyHelper or StepChange, which some may find useful when considering their wider financial position.

The options mentioned here are for general information only and are not financial advice. They form part of the wider considerations someone may take into account when reviewing their financial position and are not services provided or advised on by the Telegraph or Royal London Equity Release Advisers.

News.title: Hepatitis B
News.content:
Key facts

Hepatitis B is a viral infection that attacks the liver and can cause both acute and chronic disease

The virus is most commonly transmitted from mother to child during birth and delivery, in early childhood, as well as through contact with blood or other body fluids during sex with an infected partner, unsafe injections or exposures to sharp instruments.

Hepatitis B can be prevented by vaccines

It is estimated there are 1.2 million new infections each year and around 1.1 million deaths

Overview

Hepatitis B is a liver infection caused by a virus, which can be either short-term or long-term. Hepatitis B is a major global health concern and is most prevalent in the western Pacific, Africa and south east Asia. The infection can lead to chronic illness, significantly increasing the risk of death from cirrhosis and liver cancer.

Adults are more likely to develop the acute form of the disease, while children are more likely to have the chronic form.

Signs and symptoms

Most people do not experience any symptoms when newly infected. However, some people can have acute illness and symptoms can include:

a high temperature

tiredness

pain in the abdomen

nausea and vomiting

yellowing of the skin and whites of the eyes (jaundice)

dark urine

Dangers and complications

Most people do not have any lasting problems after having a hepatitis B infection. However, chronic hepatitis B can cause liver damage (cirrhosis) and increase the risk of getting liver cancer if left untreated. It is important to take any medicine prescribed and attend regular check-ups to ensure the liver is functioning properly.

Transmission

The virus is spread through contact with infected bodily fluids, such as blood, saliva, vaginal fluids, and semen. In areas where it is most prevalent, it is mainly spread from mother to child at birth or from an infected child to an uninfected child during the first five years of life.

Hepatitis B can also be spread through needlestick injuries, tattooing, piercing, and exposure to infected blood and body fluids. Transmission can occur through the reuse of contaminated needles and syringes.

Treatment

There is no specific treatment for acute hepatitis B. Care focuses on treating the symptom including administering fluids to prevent dehydration. Medicines, such as painkillers, can be offered to help with symptoms. Chronic hepatitis B can be treated with oral medicines, such as tenofovir or entecavir.

Treatment can slow the advance of cirrhosis, reduce cases of liver cancer, and improve long-term survival. Most people who start hepatitis B treatment must continue it for life. A liver specialist may be required to monitor the liver.

Prevention

Hepatitis B is preventable with a vaccine. In the UK babies receive three doses of the vaccine as part of the routine immunisation schedule. Babies born to mothers who have the infection receive six doses, with the first administered within 24 hours of birth. The vaccine will prevent the baby developing the disease.

Booster vaccines are not usually required for people who have completed the three-dose vaccination.

Other ways to reduce risk:

practice safe sex using condoms and reducing the number of sexual partners

avoid sharing needles or any equipment used for injecting drugs, piercing or tattooing

wash hands thoroughly with soap and water after coming into contact with blood, body fluids or contaminated surfaces

get a hepatitis B vaccine if working in a healthcare setting

use a condom

avoid sharing razors, toothbrushes and needles with others

History

While it had been recognised since the 1940s that there were two different types of hepatitis – A and B – it was the discovery of the “Australia” antigen in 1965 that kickstarted research into hepatitis. Today, it is recognised that there are five main types of the disease – A, B, C, D and E. They all cause liver disease but they differ in terms of transmission, disease severity and geographical spread, with types B and C causing the greatest disease burden.

A hepatitis B vaccine was first developed in the early 1970s and blood banks began screening donated blood for the disease at around the same time. Since 2017 all babies in the UK receive the hepatitis B vaccine as part of the routine immunisation schedule

News.title: Why are we seeing more outbreaks of the deadliest diseases?
News.content:
The other potential worry is if Ebola or Marburg mutated to be able to spread through the air – like Covid-19 or an influenza – instead of through direct contact with the bodily fluid of a victim, which slows its spread somewhat and currently renders the viruses relatively more containable.

But a strain of Ebola, known as Reston, has shown evidence of airborne transmission.

It currently is known only to infect animals, although it has repeatedly been found in the upper respiratory tract in pigs – animals that have long been regarded as one of the greatest zoonotic threats to public health because of their cells, which allow viruses to mix and mutate, creating strains capable of causing human pandemics.

There are not only more opportunities for the virus to jump from animals. Scientists are increasingly becoming aware that the virus can stay in humans long after they have recovered.

Male Ebola survivors can harbour the virus in their testicles for up to five years, representing a new potential reservoir of infection.

Yet at the same time, governments across Africa are much more prepared, says Prof David Heymann, who worked on the international response to the first outbreaks in the 1970s.

Prof Heymann, now at the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine, said governments were better at looking for the viruses, and their laboratories were much better at detecting them.

That could account for some of the increase, by recording outbreaks that would once have gone undetected, experts say.

But it is not clear.

“What’s good news is the world has definitely stepped up to surveillance and reporting, and most of these countries have got really pretty good systems now for reporting these are notable diseases and having these systems,” says Oxford’s Prof Lang.

“So that’s really excellent, but we can’t really split out whether, because we’ve not got that sort of baseline, we really can’t split out if [outbreaks] are increasing or if we’re getting better at measuring them.”

Sports.title: Europa League specialist Igor Jesus a potential needle mover as season nears dramatic climax
Sports.content:
NOTTINGHAM FOREST took another huge stride towards safety last Friday.

Vitor Pereira’s side swaggered to a 5-0 win over Sunderland at the Stadium of Light to take their total to 39 points and maintain an advantage over West Ham and Tottenham, even after both relegation rivals celebrated victories of their own on Saturday.



Morgan Gibbs-White (£4.6m) continued his fine form with another goal but it was Igor Jesus (£3.3m) who earned the most Dream Team points on Tyneside.



The Brazilian striker opened the floodgates in the 17th minute when he forced Trai Hume (£2.6m) to score an own goal with a back-post header, registering a fantasy assist in the process.

In the 34th minute, Jesus picked out Gibbs-White with a smart knock-down to make it two assists on the night.

And just three minutes later he scored a goal of his own, a composed volley, as the visitors ran riot.

With the result effectively settled, Jesus was replaced midway through the second half, by which time he had collected 14 points (despite a yellow card).

The 25-year-old now ranks eighth among Dream Team forwards with 229 points to his name, one more than Viktor Gyokeres (£4.5m).

He has scored 15 goals and provided seven assists in 2025/26 so far.

Granted, just five of his goals have come in the Premier League but he’s been prolific in the other competitions with ten goals in 12 games.



Jesus is the top scorer in the Europa League this campaign with seven goals at a strike rate of one every 88 minutes.

This Thursday, he will have the chance to add to his impressive European tally when Forest take on Aston Villa in the first leg of their semi-final at the City Ground.

Jesus is already the best-performing striker of Gameweek 33 and he has every chance of maintaining his status given Forest are one of just four teams with a second fixture to fulfil before the next deadline.

The East Midlanders will also double up in Gameweek 34.



Pereira’s side are scheduled to face Chelsea at Stamford Bridge this coming weekend before making the short trip to Villa Park for the second leg of their Europa League semi.

Dream Team bosses who took a punt on Jesus in Gameweek 33 have been handsomely rewarded and it’s not unreasonable to expect further returns in Gameweek 34.

He is currently the fifth-most popular recruit ahead of Friday’s deadline — his ownership has risen to 7.2%.

Sports.title: Steven Gerrard ‘wanted by Championship club’ as Burney face missing out on Liverpool legend
Sports.content:
BRISTOL CITY are aiming to persuade Steven Gerrard to become their next manager, according to The Independent.

The Liverpool legend, who has been working as a pundit for TNT Sports since leaving Al-Ettifaq in 2025, has also been linked to already-relegated Burnley.





Bristol, who have former England boss Roy Hodgson as interim manager, are now front-runners for the much sought-after 45-year-old coach.

They have laid out an attractive package to convince Gerrard to take the job at Ashton Gate.

After his stint in the Saudi Pro League, Gerrard is understood to be keen on a return to management.

This comes after former Three Lions team-mate Frank Lampard rebuilt his reputation in the Championship by taking Coventry City back to the Premier League.

Burnley is another possible destination, with the Clarets keen to move on from Scott Parker following an unsuccessful return to the Premier League.

According to former SunSport journalist Alan Nixon, the Clarets are considering the Liverpool legend as a potential replacement for Parker.

Should Gerrard opt for Bristol over Burnley, another candidate for the newly relegated side could be former assistant manager Craig Bellamy.

The former winger, who also played with Gerrard at Liverpool, left in 2024 to take over as Wales boss.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Gerrard last managed in England with Aston Villa in October 2022, after he guided Rangers to the Scottish Premiership title.

Bristol City are 13th in the Championship having briefly flirted with the promotion play-off places midway through the season.

The Robins were promoted to the second-tier in 2015 and have been perennial mid-table finishers for 11 years.

Starting from the 2026/27 season, play-offs in the Championship will expand to include six teams, rather than four.

EFL Chief executive Trevor Birch said: “Since their introduction in 1986/87, the play-offs have become a highlight of the domestic football calendar, capturing the drama, suspense and jeopardy that make the EFL so special.



“Following several months of discussion with clubs and other stakeholders, we are confident this change will further strengthen the Championship as a competition and give more clubs and their supporters a genuine opportunity of achieving promotion.”

Sports.title: ‘It would not have been safe’ – ‘Devastated’ footy club BANNED from play-offs after failing ground grading
Sports.content:
A NON-LEAGUE football club in the eighth tier have been relegated due to ground grading concerns.

Portishead Town, who play in the Southern League South, finished second with 95 points from 42 matches and were gearing up for Wednesday’s promotion play-off semi-final against Shaftesbury.



But instead of potentially beginning the 2026/27 season in Step 3, the Somerset-based club will play two rungs lower after a decision by the FA.



A club statement read: “Portishead Town FC is devastated to announce that, despite a remarkable performance on the pitch this season, the club will be relegated to Step 5.

“It is a bitter irony that we are now, effectively, a victim of our own success — penalised by a system that we trusted to support our rapid progress.

“This relegation follows a decision by the FA to revoke a previously granted extension until 31st July 2026. This revocation stems from ground grading concerns relating to stands not being installed by the end of March 2026.

“We wish to make it clear that stands were ordered, constructed and awaiting installation but due to outstanding unresolved health and safety matters beyond our control it would not have been safe to continue.



“We therefore asked for a small extension of time which would have seen all work completed by July 2026. This extension was refused.”

The Southern League have announced that Portishead’s appeal has been rejected.

Sixth-place finishers Bishops Cleeve, who finished 17 points behind Portishead, will take their place in the promotion play-offs.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Non-league followers are in uproar over the decision, with one writing on X: “95 points from 42 games and they’ve been arbitrarily relegated at the end of the season because … not enough seats, down you go.



“This kind of relegation surely isn’t in the spirit of a competitive pyramid?”

A Portishead fan added: “I can understand not letting us into the play-offs if they have to, but demoting us and undoing two seasons of work for the sake of a few seats is absolutely disgraceful.”

Portishead claimed they were encouraged by FA advisors to “get small things done” and “apply for an extension” and that ultimately it would be a “footballing decision”.

Eight of 10 clubs in similar positions were granted extensions, the other two were relegated solely on league position.

Portishead added in their statement: “It clearly is not (a footballing decision). Our appeal has since been rejected, a decision that feels like a betrayal of the spirit of the game.



“Regardless of local rivalries, football as a whole has lost today.”

Sports.title: Chelsea ‘make contact with Andoni Iraola’ as Blues hunt for permanent successor to sacked Liam Rosenior
Sports.content:
CHELSEA have reportedly contacted departing Bournemouth boss Andoni Iraola’s representatives as they look for a permanent successor to Liam Rosenior.

Rosenior, 41, was sacked on Wednesday after four hapless months that saw the Blues tumbling down to eighth place after a record five consecutive Premier League defeats without a goal.





Callum McFarlane was placed on interim charge until the end of the season with the West Londoners insisting there won’t be a permanent appointment before June.

According to Football London, Iraola, 43, is among the Prem giants’ candidates ahead of next season.

Chelsea have made initial contact with the Spanish tactician’s camp after he announced he will be leaving Dean Court in May after three successful years.

The Blues’ reps contacted Iraola‘s side to find out more about his plans in the summer.



Talks are not advanced as Chelsea were simply looking for more information about his current status.

Iraola has refused to discuss his future or transfer speculation as rumours suggests he will join a bigger team in the summer.

The ex-Rayo Vallecano manager has turned a lot of heads thanks to his stellar work at Bournemouth.

Iraola equalled Eddie Howe’s best ever Premier League finish last season as he led the Cherries to ninth place.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

He is now looking set to do even better this term with the team currently seventh and eyeing a maiden European qualification.

That is despite losing key players like Illia Zabarnyi, Milos Kerkez, Dean Huijsen and Dango Ouattara in the summer – before star man Antoine Semenyo’s £62.5million January move to Manchester City.

That has also led to interest from Manchester United, Liverpool, Newcastle and Crystal Palace.

United have yet to decide on their next permanent manager despite their revival under caretaker boss Michael Carrick.

The Magpies look set to miss out on European qualification, which has cast doubt on Bournemouth legend Howe’s future at St James’ Park.



Liverpool have also struggled during their title defence despite a staggering £416million transfer investment in the summer and so Arne Slot’s position has come under fire at Anfield.

And Palace will need to look for a new manager after Oliver Glasner confirmed he will leave at the end of the season.

Sports.title: Kylian Mbappe gets worrying fitness update ahead of World Cup as Real Madrid release statement
Sports.content:
REAL MADRID star Kylian Mbappe has been dealt a huge blow ahead of the World Cup.

The Frenchman has suffered a muscle injury reportedly ruling him out for the rest of the season.





Real Madrid officially confirmed the news today in a statement.

It said: “Following tests carried out today on our player Kylian Mbappé by the Real Madrid Medical Services, he has been diagnosed with a semitendinosus muscle injury in his left leg.”

Los Blancos said his recovery will be “monitored”.

He suffered the injury in Real Madrid’s 1-1 draw with Real Betis on Friday evening.



After league leaders Barcelona won on Saturday it leaves Madrid 11 points adrift of their bitter rivals in LaLiga.

With five games to go Alvaro Arbeloa’s team will need the Catalans to have a miracle-like slip up to have any chance of regaining the title and denying Barcelona a second consecutive triumph.

Mbappe looks sure to miss El Clasico on May 10 – a clash which could mathematically decide this year’s winners of the title.

The update suddenly throws the 2018 World Cup winner into a race to get fit for the 2026 tournament being held in the USA, Canada and Mexico.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

After losing to Argentina in the final despite scoring a hat-trick and scooping up the golden boot in the 2022 World Cup – the devastating Frenchman would have been seeking to go one better this year.

But we might not see Mbappe line up in France‘s new-look frontline, containing the likes of Michael Olise, Ousmane Dembele, Hugo Ekitike and Rayan Cherki.

It could be argued that France’s abundance of talent at the top will cope without the Real Madrid forward, but they are sure to want their star man at the tournament.

He has scored 24 goals in 28 LaLiga appearances this season as he leads the race for the golden boot.



The star is looking to retain the award after scoring a staggering 31 goals last term – however Mallorca’s Vedat Muriqi is on his tail with 21 goals.

Mbappe’s recent injury adds to a knock he sustained against Bayern Munich at the Allianz Arena, as the Bavarians beat Madrid 6-4 on aggregate.

He was seen wearing a plaster on his face after being caught in the previous game.

Sports.title: Huge club tipped to get RELEGATED from Premier League by data expert – and it’s not Tottenham or West Ham
Sports.content:
NEWCASTLE UNITED could still suffer a shock relegation this season, claims a data expert, despite Tottenham being the favourites for the drop.

Wolves and Burnley have already dropped down to the Championship with four games still to play.





The last relegation spot looks likely to be between Spurs and the Hammers with Nottingham Forest and Leeds both picking up points.

But stats boffin AaronW has claimed Eddie Howe‘s Magpies could still be dragged into a scrap for survival, even though they are on 42 points.

Newcastle are currently on a run of five straight defeats in all competitions and Howe might be concerned about their plight.

AaronW, who has 58,000 followers on TikTok, has presented a possible scenario where struggling Newcastle only pick up one more point and go down on goal difference.



Speaking in his TikTok video, he says: “Are we witnessing a team being relegated that no one is talking about? As I go through the games, focusing on the relegation battle, it’s not as crazy as it seems.”

His theory involves Spurs winning three of their last four games to put them on 43 points, but losing one game to Chelsea.

Newcastle crucially play Forest and West Ham in their last four games and he posed a scenario where the Magpies lost both games while drawing to Brighton.

Forest would then beat one of Chelsea, Manchester United or Bournemouth in addition to Newcastle to put them safe on 45 points.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

West Ham are predicted to continue their solid run by beating Newcastle and Arsenal but drawing to Brentford and Leeds.

AaronW’s theory continues with Tottenham beating Everton 3-2 on the final day and Newcastle losing to Fulham, which would send them down on goal difference.

The scenario is of course incredibly unlikely, especially given Opta have given Newcastle a 0.07 per cent chance of going down.



The record for relegation with the most points belongs to West Ham after picking up 42 in 2002-03.

The battle for survival looks to be a nail-biter after Tottenham ended their 118-day for a win by beating Wolves 1-0 on Saturday.

But West Ham also produced a dramatic finish to overcome Everton 2-1 in stoppage time.

Forest romped to a 5-0 win away at Sunderland on Friday and look sure to avoid the drop.

Newcastle, meanwhile, suffered a 1-0 loss away at Arsenal which means they have now lost four league games on the spin.



All of those defeats have come by a one-goal margin.

Sports.title: Bizarre moment football fan cooks steak with STRAIGHTENERS on train to Premier League clash
Sports.content:
TRAIN PASSENGERS were left stunned when a West Ham fan started cooking steak on a moving train – using HAIR STRAIGHTENERS.

Hungry Hammer Tony Goodman, 52, made the most of his four-hour journey on the Great Western Railway from St Austell, Cornwall to London Paddington.





Upon arrival, the content creator described it as the “greatest triumph of train cooking you have ever seen”.

After plugging his straighteners into the socket, bald Goodman pulled out a piece of “marinated overnight” steak with olive oil, salt and pepper.

He then placed the marinated steak between the straightener with an audible sizzle, using it as a makeshift grill, in front of two pieces of buttered bread.

As the smell of roast beef wafted through the cabin, a passenger carrying her child glanced over and laughed at the bizarre sight.

Others looks stunned at the bizarre sight as Goodman’s table seats were turned into a makeshift kitchen.

The camera then zoomed out, showing Goodman in a t-shirt with the name of Hammers legend Paolo Di Canio plastered over an altered Birra Moretti logo.

He said: “About medium rare? And there you go, there’s your cooked steak. It’s that simple.”



After topping off his steak sandwich with some mozzarella cheese, Goodman endured another comical moment.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

The straightener appeared to have overheated, jolting him off his seat.

He laughed it off, adding: “I think we’ll be sharing this sandwich, I don’t think there’s gonna be enough for two.

“I haven’t quite revolutionised train travel, but we have at least got something to eat.”

Goodman’s long trip to London proved fruitful as Nuno Espirito Santo‘s side scored a stoppage time winner to beat Everton 2-1 at the Olympic Stadium.



The result meant West Ham stayed above the relegation zone and remained two points clear of Tottenham with four games to play.

Sports.title: World Cup venue could be stripped of hosting rights due to 'appalling conditions'
Sports.content:
World Cup venue could be stripped of hosting rights due to 'appalling conditions'

FIFA has told officials from a city which is due to stage World Cup matches to make 'significant' improvements in time for the tournament - or risk losing their status as hosts

View 2 Images The 70,000-seater stadium is under scrutiny (Image: Joaquin Corchero/Europa Press via Getty Images)

A World Cup stadium could be stripped of its hosting rights after conditions were labelled 'appalling' during a major cup final. Spain's Estadio de La Cartuja in Seville staged the Copa del Rey final earlier this month, as Real Sociedad beat Atletico Madrid on penalties.

‌



Although it was Sociedad's supporters who got to enjoy the celebrations, both sets of fans were in agreement over issues getting into the ground. The 70,000 capacity stadium, which was built for the 1999 World Athletics Championships, is due to host matches at 2030 World Cup, co-hosted by six different countries.

‌



Supporters of both Sociedad and Atletico complained about the 'disastrous organisation', 'appalling conditions' and 'unimaginable chaos' when it came to entering La Cartuja. A damning report from Spanish outlet AS explains that fans had to endure long queues and gridlocked roads ahead of kick-off.

‌



In addition, the shuttle bus service which is put on for Betis supporters their home matches wasn't made available. Some fans decided to walk to the stadium which is situated around four kilometres from the city centre, an even more gruelling task during the summer months.

WORLD CUP LEGENDS: The stars who lit up football's greatest tournament - Buy the Special Edition today

FIFA to increase World Cup prize money for 48 teams after concerns raised READ MORE :

Donald Trump responds to Italy replacing Iran at the World Cup as US send clear message READ MORE :

La Cartuja is set to be Spain's fourth-biggest venue when they co-host the World Cup in four years' time. After the opening three games are played across Uruguay, Argentina and Paraguay to mark the 100th anniversary of the World Cup, Spain, Portugal and Morocco will stage the rest of the tournament.

‌



It's added in the report that FIFA has told stadium officials that 'significant' improvements are required in order for La Cartuja to keep its hosting rights, including more efficient travel infrastructure and better organisation. The Spanish FA are said to be aware of the issues and a meeting regarding the stadium's situation is being planned.

However, local authorities have described the cup final chaos as a 'one-off'. The mayor of Seville, Jose Luis Sanz, claimed that the organisation was 'reasonably good' while councillor Alvaro Pimentel added that the city's transport links to the stadium 'work very well.

What do you think of the 2030 World Cup having six co-hosts? Have your say in the comments section.

‌



View 2 Images The Estadio de La Cartuja hosted the recent Copa Del Rey final (Image: Bruno Bereau/Icon Sport via Getty Images)

As well as staging last season's Copa del Rey final between Barcelona and Real Madrid, La Cartuja hosted four matches during the European Championship in 2021, albeit with limited crowds of around 11,000 due to the global pandemic. Spain played all three of their group games in Seville before the stadium hosted Belgium's 1-0 victory over Portugal.

Scotland fans will also be familiar with the ground, as the Tartan Army played a Euro qualifier there in October 2023. La Carutja was most recently used at international level for a 2026 World Cup qualifier between Spain and Turkey in November of last year.

Sports.title: Harry Kane doesn't activate release clause as Bayern Munich make new contract move
Sports.content:
Harry Kane doesn't activate release clause as Bayern Munich make new contract move

Harry Kane is in contention for the Ballon d'Or and has been a huge success in Bavaria, with Bayern facing PSG in the Champions League semi-finals this week

View Image Bayern Munich are delighted by Harry Kane (Image: AFP or licensors)

Bayern Munich will open contract talks with Harry Kane at the end of the season as the German giants look to extend his stay beyond 2027.

‌



The England captain’s current deal expires in the summer of next year but club legend Karl-Heinz Rummenigge is desperate for Kane to stay longer.

‌



“Bringing Harry Kane to Bayern Munich was a major coup in the club’s history,” said Rummenigge, now a supervisory board member at Bayern, who face Paris Saint-Germain in the first leg of their Champions League semi-final on Tuesday night. “It is well-known that he had a release clause. He didn’t activate it, signalling that he would definitely stay in Munich.

‌



“And now, the relevant management in the operational area will hold talks with him sometime after the season, with the clear aim of extending his contract.”

Chelsea contact Andoni Iraola as Man Utd fall behind in race for Bournemouth boss READ MORE :

Kane has scored 138 goals in 141 appearances for the Bundesliga champions since moving to Munich in a £100million deal and has 53 this season.

‌



“Harry has undergone another transformation under Vincent Kompany,” Rummenigge went on. “He has always been a great striker who scored lots of goals but now he’s a playmaker, dropping back into midfield and using his wonderful long passes to bring Michael Olise and Luis Diaz into the game. That is very important for our style of play.”

While Kane is obviously enjoying his time at Bayern, there is still a suggestion he will want to return to England to try and break Alan Shearer’s record of 260 Premier League goals. Kane currently has 213. But he might feel he can still do it if he returns at the end of next season.

Meanwhile, Rummenigge also issued a hands-off warning to any Premier League club targeting former Crystal Palace attacker, Michael Olise, who has had an outstanding season with Bayern.

Article continues below

Rummenigge said: “For a player like Olise, there is no price tag that would make us flinch.”

Sports.title: Chelsea contact Andoni Iraola as Man Utd fall behind in race for Bournemouth boss
Sports.content:
Chelsea contact Andoni Iraola as Man Utd fall behind in race for Bournemouth boss

Andoni Iraola is in high demand after announcing that he will leave Bournemouth at the end of the season and Chelsea have now made their interest known after sacking Liam Rosenior

View 2 Images Andoni Iraola is attracting a lot of attention (Image: Getty Images)

Chelsea have made the first move in the race to hire Andoni Iraola by contacting the Bournemouth manager's representatives. Iraola announced earlier this month that he would step down as Cherries boss at the end of the season, putting a host of clubs on notice.

‌



The Spaniard has established a stellar reputation for his work with Bournemouth, who are seventh in the Premier League and in contention to secure European football with four games remaining. He is yet to announce his next move, with Chelsea, Athletic Bilbao, Manchester United and Crystal Palace among the clubs interested in his services.

‌



Chelsea sacked Liam Rosenior last week and, like Athletic Club, United and Palace, will appoint a new manager this summer. Calum McFarlane will continue as interim manager until the end of the season, but the BlueCo chiefs have already taken a step towards finding Rosenior's long-term successor, football.london reports

‌



The club are understood to have made contact with Iraola's representatives in an informal manner in order to assess his interest. The Blues have the 43-year-old on a shortlist of options and are yet to move much further in the recruitment process.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Iraola has already given a public response to the links. Asked whether he would be open to speaking with Chelsea, he replied: "No, I think I said it when I announced I was not continuing here. For me, now, it's about Bournemouth. Four games. We have an incredible position, (an) incredible fight (ahead).

‌



"(This) past week, you were asking me about other clubs. I don't know exactly which ones, but also, as a sign of respect for Bournemouth, I cannot talk right now about my future because it's not what worries the Bournemouth supporters."

Chelsea have moved faster than United, who are reportedly yet to reach out to potential candidates. The club's hierarchy, which includes chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox, are in no rush to make a decision on who will succeed Ruben Amorim, with Michael Carrick in the running after winning eight and drawing two of his 12 games as interim boss.

View 2 Images Andoni Iraola is yet to decide on his future (Image: (Photo by Robin Jones - AFC Bournemouth/AFC Bournemouth via Getty Images))

‌



HAVE YOUR SAY! Would Andoni Iraola be a good fit for Chelsea? Comment below.

Iraola is also on United's radar, although the vacant job at his boyhood side Athletic Club remains a distinct possibility, albeit with local reports stating that Edin Terzic is poised to replace Ernesto Valverde. If the former Borussia Dortmund coach does land that job, then Iraola could move elsewhere in his native Spain.

Previous reports have stated that is keen to move back to the country with his family after the success of three seasons with Bournemouth, where he has secured 12th and ninth-place finishes before this season, despite losing a whole host of key players.

Article continues below

The Cherries are currently unbeaten in their last 14 Premier League matches following the 2-2 draw with Leeds on the weekend. They are occupying the qualification place for the Conference League and face Palace on Sunday, before finishing their season with games against Fulham, Manchester City and Nottingham Forest.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick worry and current position as Man Utd 'settle on two candidates'
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick worry and current position as Man Utd 'settle on two candidates'

Manchester United are yet to make a decision on the appointment of their next permanent head coach, despite Michael Carrick thriving at the club on an interim basis

View 2 Images Michael Carrick could see a permanent role with Manchester United (Image: Getty Images)

Manchester United plan to go with Michael Carrick or a gettable coach with 'proven tactical acumen at the highest level' this summer. Carrick is reportedly the frontrunner for the vacant head coaching role, but with limited experience at the highest level, the Red Devils are still considering bringing in someone more seasoned.

‌



There's no denying that the Englishman has been a breath of fresh air since stepping in on an interim basis until season's end following Ruben Amorim's sacking in January. At the time of writing, United sit third in the Premier League standings, looking increasingly likely to secure Champions League football for 2026/27.

‌



However, Carrick may not be around to guide them in Europe's premier footballing competition. As per ESPN, sources have claimed that United's ideal appointment would be someone like Luis Enrique, who has consistently proven he can hang in the big leagues.

‌



Man Utd vs Brentford predictions as pundits see one outcome in Premier League clash READ MORE :

Man Utd dressing room claim says it all as Michael Carrick decision encouraged READ MORE :

The report also claims that United have no question marks surrounding Enrique's capabilities as a manager. That's given they approached him in 2022, prior to the disastrous appointment of Erik ten Hag.

With four league titles, nine domestic cups and a pair of Champions Leagues to his name from his stints in the managerial game with Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain alone, Enrique would likely walk into any team on planet earth and is the only high-profile manager with success in Europe. The likes of Andoni Iraola and Julian Nagelsmann have also been linked but their trophy cabinets pale in comparison.

However, luring the Spanish boss away from PSG could be a tough task. The Spaniard may be out of contract with Les Parisiens next summer, but reports suggest that he is poised to sign an extension which will keep him in the French capital until 2030.

‌



Settled with his current club, Enrique recently dropped a major hint that he is set to remain with PSG, at least for the new season. Speaking in a press conference on Wednesday, the 55-year-old revealed that he was already planning for the future alongside Luis Campos.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

About potential activity in the summer transfer window, he said: "There will be small adjustments, just like last year. We won't sign a lot of players."

‌



The latest will no doubt be somewhat of a worry for Carrick, whose appointment is not yet a formality despite being in pole position for the job.

Carrick will believe he's the right man to take on the gig on a full-time basis and is close to delivering what United appointed him for: Champions League football for next season.

However, an appointment wouldn't be without its risks. As things stand, the United job is Carrick's first real taste of the big leagues in a head coaching capacity.

‌



View 2 Images Luis Enrique could be a good fit for Manchester United (Image: PSG via Getty Images)

The 44-year-old enjoyed a brief caretaking role with the Red Devils in the wake of Ole Gunnar Solskjaer's departure in 2021, before moving on to Middlesbrough the following year. The Wallsend-born Premier League legend lasted three years on Teesside before he was replaced by Rob Edwards last summer.

However, with the right relationship with the board, Carrick has proven that he can compete in the English top flight with limited resources. He made no acquisitions in the January transfer window and has been highly successful with the current crop of players he inherited from Amorim.

Article continues below

So with a sizeable transfer budget to play with and a full pre-season schedule, there's no telling just how high Carrick can fly with the club he spent 12 years with as a player. He has also won the support of several club icons, with even Roy Keane admitting he hopes Carrick is given the job.

Sports.title: Steven Gerrard being eyed for Championship job - but ex-Liverpool team-mate in contention
Sports.content:
Steven Gerrard being eyed for Championship job - but ex-Liverpool team-mate in contention

Steven Gerrard is being linked with the Burnley job, which could soon become vacant as talks continue with Scott Parker following the team's relegation from the Premier League

View 2 Images Steven Gerrard is likely to be in contention for the Burnley job (Image: Molly Darlington/Getty Images)

Steven Gerrard is in contention to land the Burnley job if the newly relegated side do choose to part ways with Scott Parker.

‌



The Liverpool icon has held jobs in the Premier League and in Scotland, but never the second tier of English football. He's keen to get back into the dugout and would be among those in the frame if there was a fancy at Turf Moor.

‌



Parker has been at Burnley for two years, guiding them to promotion with 100 points, but failed to build on that as the Clarets dropped straight back into the Championship. Their relegation was confirmed last week when they lost to Manchester City.

‌



TalkSport understands that talks are ongoing over Burnley's managerial situation, with there being a realistic chance of Parker moving on. If that did happen then Gerrard would be among the leading contenders to take on the role.

Craig Bellamy, who played with Gerrard at Liverpool, would also be among the candidates. Bellamy is currently in charge at Wales, but prior to that was an assistant to Vincent Kompany at Burnley and made a strong impression.

Gerrard is now tax-exempt from his time in Saudi Arabia, having been required to remain outside of the country for a full tax year following his exit from Al Ettifaq in January 2025. He is no longer contracted to the Saudi Pro League side having stayed on after his departure as a consultant.

‌



Aston Villa was Gerrard's last job in England, before he was axed in October 2022 following just shy of a year in the job. Burnley would likely be among the favourites to come straight back up next year, possibly presenting the 45-year-old with the chance to manage in the Premier League again.

View 2 Images Scott Parker was unable to keep Burnley in the Premier League

His ex-England colleague Frank Lampard chose to step down into the Championship after several top flight roles, but has returned by virtue of getting Coventry promoted, which has seen his stock rise.

Article continues below

There are set to be a number of Premier League roles available this summer, which could see Gerrard wait before making a decision. Crystal Palace and Bournemouth have both confirmed that their managers are moving on. Marco Silva's contract at Fulham is also up when the season ends.

Sports.title: Man Utd vs Brentford predictions as pundits see one outcome in Premier League clash
Sports.content:
Man Utd vs Brentford predictions as pundits see one outcome in Premier League clash

Manchester United host Brentford in the Premier League on Monday night with pundits in agreement about one thing

View 4 Images Manchester United and Brentford are back in action at Old Trafford (Image: Jacques Feeney/Offside/Offside via Getty Images)

Manchester United meet Brentford on Monday night, with pundits adamant there's no chance of an upset this time round. United suffered a painful 2-1 loss against Leeds United in their most recent Monday night encounter, with Lisandro Martinez's red card only making matters worse.

‌



But a return to form against Chelsea last weekend has lifted spirits as Michael Carrick seeks to push the side towards European football next season. Victory over Brentford would virtually guarantee qualification for next year's Champions League.

‌



United would jump to 61 points in the Premier League standings, establishing an 11-point cushion over Brighton in fifth and cementing their third-place standing. Several of the UK's leading pundits are backing a favourable outcome for United, with Ally McCoist predicting the side will triumph to strengthen Carrick's case for the permanent role at Old Trafford.

‌



Here, Mirror Football rounds up five of the top football pundits' forecasts for Monday night's visit of Brentford.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Man Utd push ahead with transfer plan as £52m scouting trip held after Matheus Cunha chat READ MORE :

Man Utd dressing room claim says it all as Michael Carrick decision encouraged READ MORE :

Alan Shearer - United win

Alan Shearer believes that brilliance from Bruno Fernandes will be essential if United are to claim all three points at home. He told Betfair: "Man United dug out a great result last weekend, with that one bit of quality in the game when Bruno Fernandes went down to that right-hand side and pulls it back to Cunha.

‌



"That was enough to get three points against a woeful Chelsea side. I think they will have enough to beat Brentford at home, so I'm going to say a Man United home win.

"Bruno is a quality player. Where would Man United be without him? He has been the one consistent player there for so long now."

Paul Merson - Draw

View 4 Images Paul Merson can't see past a draw between the two (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

‌



Paul Merson considers a draw a fair outcome between the two sides, arguing that momentum must be maintained after a resurgent victory over the Blues. He told Sportskeeda: "Manchester United went back to normal in that game against Leeds.

"That was them under Ruben Amorim all over again, got absolutely destroyed. Although they bounced back with a win over Chelsea, they must now keep the run going.

"Brentford can cause United as much trouble as Leeds. They are a hard team to play against and if Michael Carrick's men don't start the game well, they are in trouble.

‌



"Even if Manchester United fail to get a result here, they would still be eight points ahead of Brighton in sixth-place. But United have to face Liverpool after this game and back-to-back defeats can quickly change things in the table. So this is a must-win game for them."

Criticising Carrick's recent team selections, the ex-Arsenal star added: "I did not understand why Carrick started with Benjamin Sesko in each of the last two games. I've always said that he is best when he comes off the bench.

"When things aren't going well for United, they need that option as a substitute. I hope he uses Sesko as an impact player off the bench in this game.

‌



"The way they are playing, Brighton are well and truly capable of chasing United down in the race for Champions League qualification. So they must get a win here and extend that gap over the Seagulls. I'm going for a draw here."

Harry Redknapp - United win

View 4 Images Harry Redknapp has backed United to win (Image: Malcolm Mackenzie/Getty Images)

Speaking to BetVictor, Harry Redknapp is adamant that supporters shouldn't discount Carrick from landing the full-time role. The legendary boss flagged United's tricky Monday night record, yet remains confident they'll get the job done.

‌



Redknapp said: "United are very well placed for a top four finish and that will be job done for Michael Carrick. It was a bit of a smash and grab at Stamford Bridge last week but that's a testament to the spirit he's instilled into the side. Don't rule out him getting the job in the summer.

"Brentford aren't losing, but they keep drawing! The unbeaten run is good but I'm sure Keith Andrews would have loved to have turned a few of them into wins. They've still got an outside chance of a European spot.

"United seem to play a lot on Monday night and it doesn't always go well! I think they win this though. All eyes will be on Bruno every week as he chases the assist record! He's had a brilliant season."

‌



Chris Sutton - Draw

Writing in his BBC Sport column, Chris Sutton believes United's inconsistent form could point towards yet another draw. He said: "Manchester United have become a bit unpredictable recently and Michael Carrick is another manager who could do with having a strong end to the season.

"Still, it looks like Carrick has secured Champions League football, so if the club's owners are still deciding about who will be in charge next season then he has done a more than steady job so far. It feels like he has passed his audition and also that he has a bit of clout.

"I would not like to predict what will happen about his future, though, and I am not sure how this game will go either. It should be close, and it could be quite open too. Brentford will fancy their chances after beating United 3-1 earlier in the season - and also from seeing how easily Leeds carved them open at Old Trafford a couple of weeks ago.

‌



"Igor Thiago scored twice against United in the reverse fixture, and he might cause them a problem or two again. The Bees just keep on drawing games at the moment, though, so I've really got to go for another draw here, haven't I?"

Ally McCoist - United win

View 4 Images Ally McCoist fancies United's chances at home (Image: Glyn KIRK / AFP via Getty Images)

Ally McCoist is "fancying" United to claim victory at home on Monday night. Speaking on talkSPORT BET Casino, the ex-Scotland international believes the team have sorted their defensive issues and are on the right track for Europe.

‌



McCoist said: "I fancy Manchester United at home against Brentford. They've got an efficiency about them now that they didn't have before. I know it's a stupid thing to say, but they're playing people in the positions they're accustomed to, and they just look better.

"Senne Lammens has made a big difference. What a difference he has made to that team, that feeling, they have had a makeshift defence but I thought the full-backs were excellent against Chelsea.

"Diego Dalot never gave Alejandro Garnacho a kick at the ball. Luke Shaw is consistent every week. Casemiro is solid, and Bruno Fernandes is one of the best players in the league.

Article continues below

"You've got Matheus Cunha and Bryan Mbeumo making a difference as well, with Benjamin Sesko coming in with goals. The difference in the team is absolutely remarkable, it really is.

"I expect them to win that game. They'll continue their Champions League form, and they'll get it, no problem. I think they'll be put in a position where they have to give Michael Carrick the job. I'll say 3-1 to United against Brentford."

Sports.title: Is Pep Guardiola about to quit Man City? The hints which suggest he might say goodbye
Sports.content:
Is Pep Guardiola about to quit Man City? The hints which suggest he might say goodbye

Pep Guardiola has changed the face of English football - it would be a disaster if he went and quit the Premier League this summer

View 2 Images Pep Guardiola, manager of Manchester City, celebrates after winning the Emirates FA Cup Semi Final vs Southampton (Image: 2026 Allstar)

Pep Guardiola has raised the bar and changed the face of English football since his arrival in 2016.

‌



In my view, the Manchester City boss has been the best manager of the Premier League era which includes the likes of Sir Alex Ferguson, Jose Mourinho and Arsene Wenger. Guardiola has made us change the way we think about football, brought new tactical patterns, systems, reinvented positions and led City to an incredible era of success.

‌



But there is something there that makes me think if Guardiola wins the Treble - and I think he will - then he will ride off into the sunset.

‌



Guardiola right now just looks free and, dare I say it, demob-happy, like some kind of weight has been lifted off his shoulders. Even down to that new rather trendy-looking sweatshirt with a P as a logo.

He looks carefree and is enjoying himself like never before. He looks cheeky. Enjoying more banter and managing like he knows things are coming to a glorious end.

Pep Guardiola drops huge hint he WILL be back at Man City next season READ MORE :

Gary Lineker names 'tricky' fixture that could cost Arsenal the Premier League title READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



There is also no way he signs Gianluigi Donnarumma unless he saw this season as one last hurrah. He is a keeper so out of keeping with his style. He does not want to play out from the back.

Even players coming in must ask the question: is he staying? There have always been doubts in the past few seasons. They are at an unprecedented level now.

But there is not a definitive answer, just reassurances that if the manager goes then don’t worry because the club is in good shape and will have a plan.

‌



View 2 Images Pep Guardiola led his side to a fourth straight FA Cup final (Image: 2026 The FA)

There is no doubt that City have been looking just in case. Enzo Maresca looks a good option and is being strongly tipped. It makes sense for a club to see what is out there just in case.

But I really hope Guardiola stays on and signs another deal. The point is that he has made City better and has made other teams better.

‌



When City were at their absolute peak, Liverpool had to reach incredible levels under Jurgen Klopp to win the title. Then Arne Slot did it again.

Arsenal are striving to do it but, let’s be honest, they have always had a lingering doubt that City might come back. And they have.

That’s the point: teams have to raise their game to compete with Pep. People always talk about the wages and City’s wage bill. And of course that’s a point. But it should not excuse other teams not buying well or buying efficiently. Don’t start using City as an excuse for your own failings.

‌



Guardiola gave us the inverted full back. He gave us the risk and reward of keepers playing out from the back. He’s been innovative this time with a high-press, man-to-man tactical style which outwitted their main rivals, Arsenal.

We're 10 years in and Guardiola is still at the cutting edge of football, new ideas and plans. He talked about “next season” after City’s FA Cup semi final win. A little hint he would still be around. But hardly reassuring.

‌



It would be such a shame if he went. I’m quite sure that other teams would breath a huge sigh of relief. But even if they won after his departure, it would come with the disclaimer: yeah, but it was after Pep.

Guardiola has been incredible for English football. No wonder Italy are the latest team to fancy him as a national boss. England had a go.

But I hope he stays - because he has taken the game to new levels in this country.

Sports.title: Gary Lineker's stunning Soccer Saturday revelation a year on from Match of the Day exit
Sports.content:
Gary Lineker's stunning Soccer Saturday revelation a year on from Match of the Day exit

Gary Lineker left his Match of the Day post over a year ago and he has made a surprise admission about Sky Sports' coverage.

View 2 Images Gary Lineker claimed that he watched Sky Sports' Soccer Saturday for the first time. (Image: Rest is Football)

Gary Lineker has revealed that he watched Sky Sports' Soccer Saturday for the first time this weekend. The former Match of the Day presenter admitted he was left surprised that he'd never tuned into the coverage from the broadcaster as he continues life away from the BBC flagship show.

‌



It has been 12 months since the 65-year-old officially left the hotseat after 26 years presenting the football highlights television show. The former England captain was replaced by Kelly Cates, Gabby Logan and Mark Chapman as the broadcaster made the historic move to split the coverage.

‌



Due to over a quarter of a century presenting Match of the Day, Lineker had the luxury of watching all of the top-flight action as it happened at the BBC headquarters and therefore missed the chance to watch the iconic Sky Sports show.

‌



He made the surprise admission on his podcast, The Rest is Football, he said: "Do you know what I watched yesterday? This is mad right, Gillette Soccer Saturday, I happened to switch it on for the three o'clock kick-offs.

"I was thinking to myself, 'have I ever watched this programme before?' Which sounds mad because it's been going forever.

"I was always at the Match of the Day offices watching the football so we never ever watched it, I'd seen Final Score a few times earlier this season, thought I'd watch it which is mad I've never seen that particular programme."

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Soccer Saturday first aired in 1998 and remained an integral part of supporters' weekend routines due to the popularity of the Sky Sports show.

The show has taken on numerous faces and faced the test of time throughout the decades. In recent years, the iconic faces of Jeff Stelling, Chris Kamara, Phil Thompson, Matt Le Tissier, Charlie Nicholas and Paul Merson have slowly moved away from being centre stage.

‌



Stelling left Sky Sports in 2023, and Simon Thomas has taken the post following the high-profile exit. Julian Warren has been a long-standing member of the presenting team, often stepping in during the midweek coverage.

View 2 Images Sky Sports panel of Jeff Stelling, Matt Le Tissier, Paul Merson, Phil Thompson and Charlie Nicholas (Image: Sky Sports)

Meanwhile, since leaving the BBC, Lineker has seen his Goalhanger production company go from strength to strength as statistics suggest that there are now 250,000 paying members for Goalhanger with more than 75 million downloads of its podcasts each month.

‌



Lineker will be back on mainstream television this year as part of a new game show on ITV called The Box.

He said: "I can't wait to host The Box. I've always felt right at home in the box on a football pitch, and whilst this is a different proposition, the fundamentals are similar.

"The contestants will have to quickly and masterfully work out how each game works, whilst also trying to get ahead of the competition to take control.

Article continues below

"It's going to be unpredictable and thrilling to watch, and I'm excited that I get to have a front row seat to all the action!"

Sports.title: Brundle: Happier Hamilton can still win races amid 'wide open' 2026
Sports.content:
Ferrari will be among the teams likely to make a "big step" in performance at the Miami Grand Prix as they target closing the gap to Mercedes in what will still prove a “wide open” 2026 season at front, says Sky Sports F1’s Martin Brundle.

Brundle believes that F1's return to action in the USA will be "like a relaunch of the season" after the sport's enforced April break with teams having had extended time to work on "dramatically changed and, hopefully, improved cars" with potential to shuffle the pecking order.

Mercedes will resume the campaign as clearly the team to beat after winning all three races so far with Drivers' Championship leader Kimi Antonelli and team-mate George Russell.

Ferrari and their drivers are closest to Mercedes in the standings with team-mates Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton separated by eight points in third and fourth place in the Drivers' Championship having engaged in entertaining wheel-to-wheel battles in both China and Japan.

On Hamilton, who broke his Grand Prix podium duck for Ferrari at the season's second round in Shanghai before a more difficult weekend at Suzuka when he finished sixth with Leclerc third, Brundle told Sky Sports News: "Lewis clearly enjoys these cars much more.

"Ferrari is more competitive and I think again will make a big step for Miami.

"Lewis obviously prefers this type of car to the seasons we had with the ground-effect cars that were smashing against the ground and were quite brutal things, it didn't seem to suit his style.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player With Formula 1 returning this weekend in Miami after an extended break, we look back at what happened during the first three races of the season

"But just his mood and just the way he's going about it, he just seems a lot happier because Ferrari is more competitive.

"He's got to beat Charles Leclerc if he's going to win the world championship in the other Ferrari, and others.

"Let's see if he can sustain that. If there's a sniff of a victory, I think Lewis is still very much capable of taking that."

Hamilton, when still at Mercedes, and Leclerc last won races in 2024 with Ferrari's own victory drought stretching back to October of that year, when Carlos Sainz won in Mexico City.

The season resumes with the year's second Sprint weekend in Miami, a race which McLaren have won in each of the past two seasons, although Mercedes remain favourites owing to their 100 per cent winning start to F1's new era of regulations in 2026.

But Brundle believes it is still too early in the new ruleset and car development for a definitive order to have emerged with 19 races left this season.

"I think it's totally wide open," said Brundle.

"We have got a Sprint weekend in Miami, so there are Sprint points to be won, Grand Prix points to be won.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Martin Brundle thinks Miami will feel like a relaunch to the season after rules updates and enforced break from F1

"This is going to ebb and flow. I see teams leapfrogging others with some upgrades because there is so much upside potential with these cars.

"Anybody I would say in the top four teams, any of those eight drivers, could win this year's world championship."

Sports.title: It's on! Contracts signed for Joshua vs Fury
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury are set to meet in their long-awaited heavyweight mega-fight later this year.

Joshua will come back on July 25 in a tune-up bout against Kristian Prenga and then meet his great rival Fury.

Eddie Hearn, Joshua's promoter, posted on social media: "Signed, sealed and delivered! AJ vs Fury is on!"

He described it as "the biggest piece of business we've ever done but more importantly the one we've always wanted.

"Biggest year of AJ's career coming up, the comeback is on."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Tyson Fury grabbed the mic and bellowed a challenge for Anthony Joshua to fight him next!

Fury called out Joshua after his points victory over Arslanbek Makhmudov at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium earlier this month and revealed that he had signed for the all-British mega-fight.

Ring Magazine announced the fight was a "done deal" and would take place in "Q4, 2026" in a social media post on Monday.

Hearn previously told Sky Sports that November was the date they were targeting for Joshua's fight with Fury after his July comeback bout.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Eddie Hearn revealed his plans for Anthony Joshua to fight Tyson Fury.

Joshua and Fury, two of the biggest names in British boxing, have circled one another for the best part of a decade. Fury first became a heavyweight world champion when he upset Wladimir Klitschko a decade ago. Joshua turned professional after winning Olympic gold at London 2012 and rocketed through the pro ranks.

But by the time Joshua picked up his first world title belt in 2016, Fury had stepped away from the sport.

Fury would eventually return and beat Deontay Wilder to become the WBC world champion. Joshua held the unified IBF, WBO and WBA championships and the two were close to fighting in an undisputed heavyweight championship fight.

It was not to be, Fury boxed a third fight with Wilder instead and Joshua lost to Oleksandr Usyk. The Ukrainian also defeated Fury, who retired again at the start of last year.

When Fury returned to beat Makhmudov in London earlier this month, Joshua was waiting for the all-clear to resume full training after sustaining injuries in a terrible accident in which two of his close friends and members of his team lost their lives. Joshua is now in camp working with his former rival Usyk, who has backed AJ to beat Fury.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player 'AJ will beat Fury!' | Usyk on 'helping' Joshua in camp

With one more hurdle to clear for Joshua, Kristian Prenga on July 25, the two rivals will finally box in the most richly anticipated heavyweight bout the UK will have ever seen.

The exact date and location of the contest is yet to be confirmed but hopes will be high for another British stadium fight.

Fury vs AJ... and a Dua Lipa concert?

Sky Sports Boxing expert Andy Scott says:

"If you go to each part of this deal, everyone is saying the same thing: that Anthony Joshua will fight Tyson Fury this year.

"I've spoken to Spencer Brown from Gold Star promotions - who represents Tyson Fury - and he says 'go ahead and confirm it'.

"Tyson Fury came back successfully from his own retirement - he confirmed after the Arslanbek Makhmudov fight that he had signed his part of the deal.

"There was a little bit of disappointment that Joshua didn't join him in the ring and confirm that fight on the night.

"According to Turki, Spencer Brown, and Eddie Hearn that fight is done.

"There are lots of things still to go through. There isn't a confirmed venue, and AJ still needs to go through his own comeback fight. Brown has confirmed that it's a two-fight deal.

"I don't know if they're pulling my leg here, but I'm hearing that Turki has stipulated that Dua Lipa needs to perform at the fight! If you're listening, Dua, clear your diary!

"We aren't there yet - but we are very close now. AJ needs to come through his next fight, and then all roads lead to Joshua vs Fury next year."
